name: hashid
one_line: identify the type of a hash
plain: `hashid` looks at a hash (a long scrambled string) and tells you which hash algorithms it could be: MD5, SHA-1, NTLM, bcrypt and so on. It is the question you ask before cracking: which mode do I tell john or hashcat to use?

It cannot be sure, because many hashes look alike (MD5 and NTLM are both 32 hex characters). It lists the candidates in order, and with -m and -j it prints the matching hashcat mode number and john format.
when: Identify an unknown hash from a challenge.
Find the hashcat mode (-m number) or john format to use.
Check a whole file of hashes.
Spot special formats such as $2y$ (bcrypt) or $6$ (sha512crypt).

examples.title: Identify one hash
examples.explain: Quote the hash. Output lists possible types: MD5 first, then others of the same length.

examples.title: Show hashcat modes
examples.explain: -m adds the hashcat mode number to each guess: use it as hashcat -m NUMBER.

examples.title: Show john formats
examples.explain: -j adds the john format name for --format=.

examples.title: From a file
examples.explain: If the argument is a file, every line is analysed.

examples.title: Save the result
examples.explain: -o writes the report to a file.

options.plain: A hash string or a file of hashes.
List all hash types, including rare ones.
Show the hashcat mode number for each match.
Show the john the ripper format for each match.

mistakes: Believing the first guess blindly: 32 hex characters can be MD5, NTLM or others.
Forgetting the salt or extra fields (user:hash:salt) and passing the whole line.
Not quoting a hash that contains $: the shell expands it. Use single quotes.
Passing a hash with a trailing newline or space.
try: Hash 'password' with md5sum and run hashid on the result.
Run hashid -m on a $6$ hash from /etc/shadow.
Use the mode number with hashcat on a hash you made.
see_also: hash-identifier(1), john(8), hashcat(1), md5sum(1), sha256sum(1), name-that-hash.
captured_with: Examples are written to explain a technique; they are not captured output.
